title: A superlogarithmic saving for Oddtown modulo composite numbers
summary: Let $f_{\ell}(n)$ be the largest size of a family $\mathcal{A}\subseteq2^{[n]}$ such that no member has size divisible by $\ell$, while the intersection of every two distinct members has size divisible by $\ell$, and let $ω(\ell)$ denote the number of distinct prime divisors of $\ell$. For any prime power $\ell$, the classical answer is $f_{\ell}(n)=n$. When $ω(\ell)\geq 2$, Bukh, Chao, and Zheng recently proved $ω(\ell)n-O_{\ell}\left(n^{\frac{ω(\ell)-2}{ω(\ell)-1}}(\log n)^{C_{\ell}}\right)\leq f_{\ell}(n)\leqω(\ell)n-2ω(\ell)\log n+11$ for some $C_{\ell}>0$.
